en: The Banaue Rice Terraces use the inclined plane simple machine to reduce the effort needed to farm steep mountains.
The wooden wheels of a traditional Philippine kalesa act as wheel and axle simple machines to move passengers.
The flagpole at Rizal Park uses a fixed pulley to change the direction of force when raising the flag.
Tokay geckos use friction from millions of tiny hairs on their feet to climb smooth vertical walls.
Gravity pulls falling volcanic rocks from Mount Mayon downward toward the Earth's center during an eruption.
The Philippines has large deposits of magnetite, a highly magnetic iron ore that is strongly attracted to magnets.
The Malitbog Geothermal Power Plant in Leyte converts thermal energy from underground heat into electrical energy for the grid.
The Cape Bojeador Lighthouse in Ilocos Norte uses special glass lenses to refract and focus light into a strong beam.
The Las Piñas Bamboo Organ produces sound when air vibrations travel through its unique bamboo pipes.
Magma beneath Taal Volcano transfers thermal energy to the surrounding cooler rocks through the process of conduction.
Water stored behind the San Roque Dam possesses gravitational potential energy before spinning the electricity generators.
A working carabao converts chemical energy from digesting grass into kinetic energy to plow the muddy rice fields.
